title: Autumn Road Trip: Ksamil Butrint and Blue Eye by Car
excerpt: Discover how to explore Ksamil, the UNESCO site of Butrint and the stunning Blue Eye in autumn, with a comfortable drive from Tirana Airport.
intro: When the summer crowds fade and the air turns crisp, southern Albania becomes a perfect playground for a relaxed road adventure. Starting at Tirana Rinas Airport, you can follow a scenic route to the turquoise bays of Ksamil, the ancient ruins of Butrint, and the mysterious spring known as the Blue Eye.

sections.title: Ksamil Butrint and Blue Eye by Car: Route Overview
sections.body: The journey begins by picking up your rental from AutoConnect at Tirana Airport and heading south on the SH4. The drive to Ksamil covers roughly 270 km and takes 4 to 4.5 hours, depending on whether you choose the coastal Llogara Pass for breathtaking views or the faster inland highway via Gjirokastër. From Ksamil, Butrint National Park lies just 5 km away, and the Blue Eye is a short 22 km drive from Sarandë. This compact loop lets you see the three highlights comfortably in one day.

sections.title: Scenic Options: Llogara Pass vs Inland Highway
sections.body: If you enjoy winding roads and sea panoramas, the Llogara Pass adds about 30 minutes but rewards you with cliffs dropping into the Ionian Sea. The inland route through Gjirokastër is flatter and quicker, ideal for those who prefer a smoother ride and want extra time at the sites. Autumn brings clear skies, so either choice offers excellent visibility. Remember to check weather forecasts; occasional fog can appear in the mountain pass early in the morning.

sections.title: Visiting Butrint National Park
sections.body: Butrint sits only 5 km south of Ksamil, making it a 10‑minute drive. A spacious parking lot sits right at the park entrance, free for visitors. From there, a well‑signposted path leads to the UNESCO‑listed ruins, where you can explore Roman theatres, Byzantine basilicas, and the ancient acropolis. Autumn temperatures between 15 °C and 24 °C are perfect for walking the trails without the summer heat, and the reduced visitor numbers let you linger at the most photogenic spots.

sections.title: Exploring the Blue Eye (Syri i Kaltër)
sections.body: The Blue Eye is located about 22 km north of Sarandë. Park at the main gate—there is a modest paid lot with space for cars and buses. From the parking area, a 1.5 km shaded trail leads to the spring, where the water erupts from a deep, crystal‑blue pool. The autumn light creates vivid reflections, and the cooler air makes the short hike pleasant. Bring a light jacket; evenings can drop to 15 °C.

sections.title: Practical Tips for Autumn Driving
sections.body: Autumn roads are generally in good condition, but be prepared for occasional rain on the coastal stretch. Keep a spare tire and a basic emergency kit in the car. Fuel stations become less frequent past Gjirokastër, so fill up before you leave Tirana. Using a GPS or a reliable offline map helps navigate the rural sections where signage may be sparse. Finally, respect local speed limits—80 km/h on highways and 50 km/h in villages.

tip.title: Pro Tip: Sunrise at Llogara Pass
tip.body: Leave Tirana before 7 am and drive the Llogara Pass early to catch the sunrise over the Adriatic. The light is spectacular for photos, and the road is quiet before the midday traffic builds.

faq.question: Can you easily visit Ksamil, Butrint, and the Blue Eye by car in a single day?
faq.answer: Yes. The three sites form a compact loop: 4‑4.5 hours from Tirana to Ksamil, a 10‑minute drive to Butrint, and another 22 km to the Blue Eye. With an early start you can comfortably explore each location and still have time for a relaxed lunch.

faq.question: What are the parking options at Butrint National Park and the Blue Eye?
faq.answer: Butrint offers a large free parking lot right at the entrance. The Blue Eye has a small paid lot near the main gate; from there you walk 1.5 km on a marked trail to the spring. Both areas are well‑signposted and suitable for rental cars.

faq.question: Is the drive from Tirana to Southern Albania safe for international tourists in autumn?
faq.answer: The SH4 highway is paved and regularly maintained. Autumn weather is mild, but occasional rain can make mountain sections slippery. Driving a well‑maintained rental, keeping an eye on weather updates, and respecting speed limits ensures a safe journey for visitors.
